fixes.explanation: Good guess, friend, because those names do show up in Numbers. Joshua and Caleb are two of the men who explored the land, and they urged Israel not to be afraid (Numbers 14:6, 9). But in this passage, the finders bring the man to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). No elders are named here. So the whole camp is about to find out what's going on, not just a couple of familiar faces.

Right on the money, baker. The text says that because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody (Numbers 15:34). He was held while the question was still open. Think of a batch sitting in the oven with the timer still running. Nobody pulls it out until the time is up, and nobody decided early.

Yes, baker, you caught it. God says the tassels are so they may remember the commandments of the LORD and obey them, "…and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes." (Numbers 15:39) The tassels point away from following their own heart and eyes, not toward it. It's a tricky one, because the verse names the heart and eyes right at the end, and that's easy to grab onto.

Edom is a place that comes up elsewhere in the Bible, but it's not the one God names here. He says He is the LORD their God "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Numbers 15:41) Egypt is the land He names.
